summary: German WWI veteran and convicted child rapist Oskar Dirlewanger led an SS penal unit of poachers and criminals that massacred tens of thousands of civilians in Belarus and Warsaw's Wola district from 1940 to 1944.

evidence.note: birth in Wurzburg introduced; childhood moves to Stuttgart and Esslingen follow
long background segment on corporal punishment of children in Wilhelmine Germany
WWI service as machine gunner on the Western Front via Belgium into France
postwar use of armored trains to crush communist uprisings; Beer Hall Putsch support
1934 conviction for raping a 14-year-old Red Cross volunteer; prison and camp
rehabilitated by serving with the Condor Legion in Spain, 1937-1939
unit sent to the Lublin district in 1940; looting and guarding camp construction
transfer to Belarus; village burnings and death zones killing tens of thousands
gay men, criminals and political prisoners forced into the penal unit
Wola massacre during the 1944 Warsaw Uprising; hospital rapes and executions
beaten to death in French-run custody by Polish guards, June 1945

notes: Episode title misspells the name; subject uses the standard spelling Oskar Dirlewanger. Transcript garbles the birth date and calls Wurzburg Swabian; lifespan 1895-1945 from known facts. Transcript places the Slovak uprising operation in Hungary; it was in Slovakia, given only a passing mention so SK left out of setting. WWI Eastern Front service is brief and unspecific, so no eastern country added.
